::: embed-page-body

Most research on representation bias treats electoral institutions as a single bundle. *Distorted Democracies* (Beramendi, Boix, Guinjoan &amp; Rogers) instead isolates one institution — **malapportionment**, the mismatch between the share of seats and the share of votes or population allocated to each district — and asks how much of the total gap between voters and their parliament it actually explains, and in which ideological direction it pulls.

To do this, the paper compiled a new dataset covering **more than 20,000 districts and 1,100 parties across 65 democracies (1996–2020)**, in both lower and upper chambers, and pooled it with Spanish survey data (N=488,000) to trace how voters' preferences translate — or fail to translate — into representation.

### Four building blocks of representation bias

REPBIAS decomposed the total gap between the ideological centre of the electorate and that of the elected legislature — **Total Representation Bias (TRB)** — into the distinct institutional sources that produce it:

::::::: insight-grid
::: {.insight-card .surface-card}
<span class="insight-icon">🗳️</span>

#### MRB
**Malapportionment Representation Bias.** The share of the total bias caused specifically by the mismatch between seats and votes/population across districts — the focus of this page.
:::

::: {.insight-card .surface-card}
<span class="insight-icon">📐</span>

#### SRB
**Seat Representation Bias.** The bias jointly produced by district magnitude and the seat-allocation formula — the dominant source of distortion in most systems (see [Decomposing Bias](decomposing-bias.qmd)).
:::

::: {.insight-card .surface-card}
<span class="insight-icon">🚧</span>

#### ThRB
**Threshold Representation Bias.** The bias produced specifically by the legal electoral threshold a party must clear to win seats.
:::

::: {.insight-card .surface-card}
<span class="insight-icon">Σ</span>

#### TRB
**Total Representation Bias.** MRB + SRB + ThRB — the overall gap between what voters wanted and who ended up representing them.
:::
:::::::

SRB and ThRB were isolated through controlled simulation (see [Decomposing Bias](decomposing-bias.qmd)); the map below shows what *Distorted Democracies* measured directly and empirically, country by country: malapportionment itself, and its associated MRB and TRB.

### Headline findings

- Malapportionment is **larger in upper than in lower chambers** — second chambers are where the institution really bites.
- Contrary to the received wisdom (often shaped by cases like Spain), malapportionment is **ideologically neutral in most lower-house elections** worldwide: where a detectable bias exists, it favours the left about as often as the right.
- **Upper chambers show a sharper, one-directional asymmetry**: a rightward bias predominates, and among the strongest cases, it is exclusively rightward.

:::
